    01 · A stronger decision document

    Make the case. Test the case.

    Bring a product strategy, proposal, or decision memo. Examine the claims that matter, connect them to evidence, and see which unresolved questions could change the recommendation.

    The planned experience keeps the document at the center. Every review should lead to a useful next step: supply evidence, revise the recommendation, or make the uncertainty explicit.

    Write Capture the problem and the decision you are proposing.

    Examine Inspect a claim, its evidence, and what remains uncertain.

    Revise Preview a change and consider the conclusions it affects.

    Share Explain your recommendation and what could change it.

    02 · Rigorous reasoning

    Catch the weakness before the meeting.

    A polished paragraph can still rest on a weak assumption. Diyalamp’s planned review experience focuses on the few questions that could materially change your product decision.

    Pull on a claim.

    Distinguish an observation from an explanation. See whether the evidence supports what you are saying, and examine a more precise formulation.

    A claim proportionate to its support.

    Change a premise. Follow the consequences.

    When an assumption changes, see which recommendations may need another look. You choose what to revise.

    A coherent argument after each change.

    Give the argument shape.

    Use an optional story spine to rearrange the ideas in your memo. Preview the structure before accepting it.

    A clear path for your reader.

    Ask what would change your mind.

    Examine the strongest alternative, a pivotal uncertainty, or the evidence that would reverse your recommendation.

    A decision that can be reconsidered.

    03 · Organizational culture

    Build a culture of defensible decisions.

    Move from one well-reasoned memo to a shared product practice. Make claims traceable, alternatives visible, and uncertainty explicit across your team.

    The long-term vision is an organizational home for writing standards and decision rationale, so teams can understand why a choice was made and when to revisit it.

    Rigor should help people think. It should never become a document quota, an employee score, or another approval checklist.

    An open foundation

    Reasoning you can inspect.

    The open-source engine organizes review around framing, evidence, reasoning, alternatives, and an explicit decision. The planned product turns that foundation into a useful writing experience.

    AI findings can be wrong. Authors must be able to inspect, challenge, and dismiss them. This approach does not guarantee a correct business outcome.

    Explore the open-source engine
    What can I use today?

    The interactive pricing-memo example on this page and the open-source engine. Hosted review, accounts, subscriptions, and team workflows are still in development.

    Will Diyalamp write the decision for me?

    The aim is to help you develop and test your reasoning. Proposed edits should be visible, reversible, and accepted by you. The final decision stays yours.

    Is this only a document editor?

    The initial commercial focus is reviewing consequential product documents. A calm writing experience and shared organizational standards are part of the broader direction.

    Does defensible mean defending my original position?

    No. A strong review can change the recommendation. The goal is a decision proportionate to the evidence, including honest uncertainty and the strongest alternative.
